podcast.title: Maynard James Keenan's Family Winemaking Heritage
podcast.body: Maynard James Keenan, known for his work in Tool, A Perfect Circle, and Puscifer, has a family history in winemaking, with relatives in northern Italy who he believes still make wines. This heritage influenced his own venture into viticulture. "His family still might make wines in northern Italy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Maynard's Other Band
podcast.body: Puscifer is Maynard James Keenan's other musical project, active during periods when he was not working with Tool. "When he wasn't working with Tool, Maynard had his other band, Pussifer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Merkin Vineyards and Caduceus Cellars – Maynard James Keenan's Arizona Wine Operations
podcast.body: Maynard James Keenan owns Merkin Vineyards and Caduceus Cellars, high-end wine operations located in the Sedona area of Arizona, specifically in Cornville, north of Phoenix and south of Flagstaff off I-17. He invested money earned from Tool and A Perfect Circle into these ventures. Merkin refers to a wig worn in the pubic region, while Caduceus, the ancient symbol for commerce, is associated with the brand's website, www.cadocious.org. His wines, particularly the '84 cab blend, have received excellent reviews, and the tasting center invites wine lovers to sample and purchase. "Maynard owns Merckin Vineyards."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tom Morello Guest Appearance
podcast.body: Tom Morello has made guest appearances on Puscifer's records. Puscifer is described as the "toolside project," implying a connection to the band Tool. "He makes guest appearances on his friends records, the prodigy, the day Matthew's band, Anti-Fly, Pusifer, the toolside project."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Survival of Tracks as "Tapeworm DNA"
xref.body: Despite the Tapeworm album never being officially released, two tracks are noted to carry its "DNA": "Passive" on A Perfect Circle's 2004 album "Emotive" (a descendant of a song called "Vacant"), and "Potions" which appeared on a Puscifer album. These releases offer glimpses into the material created during the project. "Two release tracks do have tapeworm DNA, though. One is called passive. It's on a perfect circle's 2004 album, Emotive. It's a descendant from a song called Vacant. Another is Potions, which appeared on a pusifer album."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
